第 41 章 How to Be Discerning Without Being Invalidating如何有洞察力而不否定别人

Akash Bhalla / 阿卡什·巴拉

— 第 124 页 —

First, some context: I'm at my company's 2017 Christmas party. It's a relatively classy affair. We're on a boat cruising along the Thames while people mingle and talk, enjoying the faux casino that's been set up on board. I'm at the bar chatting with Samantha, our head of people, and the conversation turns toward hiring. Sam asks if I'd had the opportunity to speak much with one of our newer hires. I tell her I haven't. She tells me I should; we'd get on very well, she feels, particularly because of my personality — I'm "very cynical." I'm pretty sure it was meant as a compliment, akin to being realistic or discerning; however, it sticks with me and I can't help but return to the thought over the next few weeks. I'm cynical.

先给点背景：我在公司 2017 年圣诞派对上。那是个比较高级的场合。我们在泰晤士河上的一艘游船上，人们互相寒暄聊天，享受船上的模拟赌场。我在吧台和我们的人力负责人 Samantha 聊天，话题转到招聘。Sam 问我有没有机会和某个新员工多聊聊。我说没有。她告诉我应该聊；她觉得我们会合得来，特别是因为我的性格——我「很愤世嫉俗」。我很确定这是想夸我，类似于说我现实或有洞察力；然而这句话一直缠着我，接下来几周我忍不住反复想这件事。我很愤世嫉俗。

Being Realistic现实一点

I'd like to think I'm realistic (or pessimistic?), not cynical. In some ways, realism is a fundamental quality of good software engineers. A keen eye for detail and a methodical, logical approach to problems. Being able to connect to the reality of a situation and planning accordingly. Although a more optimistic or hopeful person might see a feature or requirement and think of all the problems that it will solve, the eagle-eyed engineer will look at it and think of all the scenarios in which it will fail.

我愿意认为我是现实的（或者悲观的？），不是愤世嫉俗的。在某些方面，现实感是好软件工程师的基本品质。对细节的敏锐眼光和有条理、有逻辑的问题处理方式。能够连接到情境的现实并据此计划。虽然一个更乐观或充满希望的人看到一个功能或需求会想到它能解决的所有问题，眼光锐利的工程师会看着它想到它会失败的所有场景。

— 第 125 页 —

Both are essential, of course. You need hopeful optimism to build a vision of a better future, and you need grounded realism to achieve it. When harnessed correctly, this "grounded realism" can be extremely powerful and useful. As a developer, it's a useful skill for focusing in on edge cases and "sad paths" when building a feature or analyzing a codebase or system. It also helps in accurately scoping a piece of work and building a reliable product.

两者当然都是必不可少的。你需要充满希望的乐观来建设更美好未来的愿景，你需要脚踏实地的现实来实现它。当正确驾驭时，这种「脚踏实地的现实」可以非常强大和有用。作为开发者，在构建功能或分析代码库/系统时关注边界情况和「悲伤路径」是一项有用的技能。它还有助于准确界定工作范围和构建可靠产品。

The Danger of Being Too Realistic太现实的危险

This ability or quality of being realistic has its value when applied to a work context, as just mentioned. However, it's a slippery slope, and this mentality can easily lead to you becoming overly judgmental and critical of other people's choices. You begin to assume that your way of thinking is the only one of any value, and other approaches or styles are invalid.

这种现实的能力或品质在工作场景中应用时有其价值，如前所述。然而这是一个滑坡，这种心态很容易导致你变得过度评判和批评别人的选择。你开始假设你的思维方式是唯一有价值的，其他方法或风格都是无效的。

I have found this a difficult transition as my role has changed. I spent a decade as a software developer and honed my ability to think in terms of code and logic, spotting edge cases in a world that is pretty black and white and failure is more binary. But I have now moved into a head-of-engineering role that is much more focused on people and management, where the scope goes beyond the system and code, and there are more shades of gray.

随着角色变化，我发现这是一个艰难的转变。我做了十年软件开发者，磨练了用代码和逻辑思考的能力，在一个相当黑白分明、失败更二元的世界里发现边界情况。但我现在转到了一个更关注人和管理的工程负责人角色，范围超越了系统和代码，有更多灰色地带。

An immediate example comes to my mind. We run a regular book club at work themed around management and leadership; the current book we're all reading is Legacy, by James Kerr. I've never read it before, but some members of the team are big fans, and it is one of Sam's favorite books. I strongly disliked the book, and it took considerable effort to get through it. My first instinct was to be aggressively dismissive and critical of the book without regard for other people's opinion. It was only after being challenged that I realized what I was doing.

我脑子里立刻想到一个例子。我们在公司有一个定期读书俱乐部，主题是管理和领导力；现在大家在读 James Kerr 的《Legacy》。我以前没读过，但团队一些成员是它的粉丝，也是 Sam 最喜欢的书之一。我非常不喜欢这本书，花了很大力气才读完。我的第一反应是激进地否定和批评这本书，不管别人的意见。直到被挑战后我才意识到自己在做什么。

Yes, I disliked the book; it clearly wasn't something that I enjoyed or that resonated with me. Yet, it was equally clear that others had the complete opposite reaction to it; they found it inspiring and captivating. There is nothing wrong with the book. There is nothing wrong with the people who liked it. There is nothing wrong with me. There is just a mismatch, and that's fine. The book isn't written for people like me, but that doesn't make it inherently bad. I need to learn to stop and think before rushing to criticize something and instead try to recognize and appreciate that I might just not be the intended audience.

是的，我不喜欢这本书；它显然不是我享受或共鸣的东西。然而同样清楚的是，其他人对它有完全相反的反应；他们觉得它鼓舞人心、引人入胜。书没有错。喜欢它的人没有错。我没有错。只是不匹配而已，这没关系。这本书不是写给像我这样的人看的，但这并不意味着它本质上不好。我需要学会在急于批评某件事之前停下来思考，而是努力认识和欣赏我可能只是不是目标读者。

— 第 126 页 —

It's the difference between: "This is s---." and: "This isn't for me."

区别在于：「这是屎。」和：「这不是给我的。」

Adapting to a New Role适应新角色

With this shift in my role, I'm learning that the most important thing for me is no longer being able to spot edge cases and failure scenarios from a hundred paces. There are far more skilled developers than me working here that can do that. My focus now needs to be on creating a validating environment at work in order to nurture the people and the culture of the organization. I need to learn to maintain an ability to be discerning yet balance that with an ability to encourage and nurture.

随着角色的转变，我在学习对我来说最重要的不再是百步之外发现边界情况和失败场景。这里有比我技术好得多的开发者能做这个。我现在的焦点需要放在创造一个验证性的工作环境来培养人和组织文化。我需要学会保持洞察力，同时平衡鼓励和培养的能力。

Squashing bugs and inefficiencies when building a product is a skill to be proud of. Squashing ideas, dreams, and opinions is not.

在构建产品时消灭 bug 和低效是值得骄傲的技能。消灭想法、梦想和意见则不是。
